findings.title: Every functional and technical success criterion has a covering task
findings.description:
Cross-reference against `268-slice.pure-cf-build.md` Success Criteria:

- FR1 (no reads/writes of `adoption.state`, no detection, no `sq` spawn on the three surfaces) → task 5.1 purity test (snapshot, `Adoption Facts` absence, `sq` marker absence across CLI/`context_build`/`template_preview`).
- FR2 (Phase 0 brownfield returns concept prompt and writes nothing for any stored state) → task 5.1 (CLI path runs once with no `.context-forge.toml`, once with `in_progress`).
- FR3 (greenfield / already-planned / later-phase byte-identical) → task 2.1 + 2.2 golden capture and comparison, gated again at 3.7 and 6.1.
- FR4 (CLI/MCP `context_build` parity) → task 5.1 parity check.
- FR5 (`MIN_GUIDE_VERSION` warning preserved on stderr / separate MCP item) → tasks 3.5, 3.6, 6.1 guide-warning success clause.
- TR1 (`services/` imports nothing from `adoption/` or `detection/`) → grep checks at 3.3 and 6.2.
- TR2 (no orphan exports; `history` / `comprehensionAnalysis` / `adoptionOutcome` retained for 269/271) → 6.2 export audit, with the exception listed.
- TR3 (format/lint/typecheck/tests pass) → 6.1 full pass; format is ESLint per the context summary.
- IR (269 starts with no build-path code to change) → implicitly covered by 4.x keeping `adoptionOutcome` and the read path of `adoptionState`, plus the 6.2 export audit.

The Migration Plan table from the design maps one-to-one onto the deletes in sections 3 and 4.

findings.title: Sequencing is correct and dependencies are respected
findings.description: Order: branch (1) → golden capture on unmodified source (2) → render removal that keeps the signature (3.1–3.2) → seam removal that changes signatures (3.3–3.6) → code deletion (4) → purity test (5) → full validation (6). The seam removal is split into two commits (3.2a and 3.7) at exactly the points where the workspace is green, and the `core` rebuild dependency between 3.4 and 3.5 is called out. No circular dependencies.

findings.title: Test-with pattern is respected
findings.description: Every implementation edit that requires test updates names the corresponding test file in the same task (3.1, 3.2, 3.3, 3.5, 3.6, 4.1, 4.3, 4.4). The new behavior test (golden) is created alongside its fixtures (2.1 + 2.2). The replacement integration test (5.1) is its own task and follows the `adoptionParity.test.ts` deletion in 3.6, with a `git show {target}:…` recipe to recover the pattern.

findings.title: Commit markers sit at working, tested points
findings.description: Commits at 2.3 (golden captured before edits), 3.2a (render removal compiles + tests), 3.7 (seam removal compiles + tests), 4.1–4.4 (one deletion each, with typecheck/test gates), 5.1 (purity test passes), and a conditional commit at 6.3 if 6.2 / 6.3 surfaces residual items. No commit-after-every-task bloat; no "everything at the end" anti-pattern.

findings.title: Proportionality fits the slice
findings.description: Six tasks for a multi-package cut that touches `core`, `cli`, `mcp-server` plus tests. Each task's step count is justified (e.g. 5.1 is effort 3 because the purity test is the load-bearing behavior proof; 3.x splits a 2-commit seam removal into clearly marked sub-units because the workspace would not compile midway otherwise). No excess test scaffolding beyond what the success criteria require: the golden test, the purity test, and the test edits needed to keep the suite green.

findings.title: Retention list is honored
findings.description: `AdoptionError`, `readAdoptionState`, `decideOutcome`, `BROWNFIELD_MIN_SOURCE_LINES`, every `detection/` module except `squadronProbe.ts`, `COMPREHENSION_PROFILE_VARIABLE` / `findComprehensionAnalysis`, `core/tests/helpers/adoptionFixtures.ts`, and `core/tests/fixtures/brownfield-guide` are all either explicitly preserved (4.2, 4.3, 4.4) or named as the fixture used by 2.1 / 5.1. `COMPREHENSION_PROFILE_VARIABLE` is the explicit exception in the 6.2 grep, matching the design's D4 note.

findings.title: `adoptionStateWrites: 'read-only'` in 2.2 is a no-op for the captured cases
findings.description: The golden capture passes `{ adoptionStateWrites: 'read-only' }`, but the two fixtures (greenfield and already-planned) do not trigger adoption logic, so the option has no effect on the captured output. The "for now" wording in the task may mislead a junior implementer into thinking the option matters for byte-identity. Functionally harmless — the golden still reflects post-cut behavior — but worth knowing in case the implementer spends time investigating.

structured_findings.summary: Every functional and technical success criterion has a covering task
Sequencing is correct and dependencies are respected
Commit markers sit at working, tested points
